question.text: On March 30, 1981, this man shot Ronald Reagan in an attempt to impress Jodie Foster, but failed to kill him.
question.clue: Following this man's most notable action, his victim allegedly joked "I hope you're all Republicans" to his doctors.

swap.text: This president supported Don't Ask, Don't Tell at the time and also signed the Defense of Marriage Act in 1996. He later became involved in a scandal involving a White House Intern, Monica Lewinsky.
swap.clue: Notable monarchs with this given name include one who was fatally shot by Walter Tirel and one who suffered a postmortem stomach rupture at his funeral due to an incorrectly sized coffin.

question.text: During the Katrina benefit concert, this man went off-script to controversially state "George Bush doesn't care about black people."

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the Watergate Scandal.
swap.text: During the Saturday Night Massacre, the resignation of Attorney General Elliot Richardson and Deputy Attorney General William Ruckelshaus led to Cox being fired by this Solicitor General. Ronald Reagan attempted but failed to nominate this man to the Supreme Court in 1987.
swap.clue: As Solicitor General, this man ultimately carried out Nixon's order to fire special prosecutor Archibald Cox.

question.text: This centrist Maine Republican co-sponsored the stand-alone repeal bill along with Connecticut Independent Democrat Joe Lieberman. In spite of heavy lobbying, this senator's Maine colleague Olympia Snowe had voted against the Defense Authorization Act because Majority Leader Reid would not allow Republican amendments.
question.clue: This senator voted to acquit President Clinton after a co-proposal with Olympia Snowe to separate the charge and the remedy failed and in September 2015 this senator cast their 6,000th consecutive vote.

swap.leadin: This senator shocked his fellow Republicans by voting against the Health Care Freedom Act, which was intended to replace the Affordable Care Act.
swap.text: Name this Republican Senator from Arizona who passed away in August, 2018. In 2008, he ran unsuccessfully for the presidency against Barack Obama.
swap.clue: At one campaign stop, this man was booed for correcting an audience member who called his opponent, Barack Obama, an Arab.

question.leadin: Ted Kennedy claimed that this man's America would be one where "women would be forced to get back-alley abortions" and "blacks would sit at segregated counters."
question.text: Name this ultra-conservative Supreme Court justice nominee, whose controversial confirmation hearing led to his name becoming a byword for getting put down through ad hominem attacks.
question.clue: This man performed an action that William Ruckelshaus and Elliot Richardson refused to do, the firing of Archibald Cox in the Saturday Night Massacre, while serving as Solicitor General.

swap.text: This former Congresswoman from the Eighth District of Arizona started the Americans for Responsible Solutions PAC [pack] to advocate against gun violence after she was shot in the head at a Safeway near Tucson in 2011.
swap.clue: She received a standing ovation from Congress when she appeared to cast a vote in August 2011.

question.text: In March 2011, this former IRA champion from New York's 3rd district and chairman of the Committee on Homeland Security stirred up controversy by holding hearings into the radicalization of American Muslims.

swap.leadin: Identify these alums of Mount Holyoke.
swap.text: This 1975 alumna in economics became the first Asian-American woman appointed to a Cabinet position, namely Secretary of Labor by George W. Bush.
swap.clue: This Taiwan-born politician was the first Chinese American to be appointed to a President's Cabinet, serving as Secretary of Labour for the entire Bush Administration.

question.text: This Health and Human Services Secretary under Barack Obama was defendant in the 2012 Supreme Court case that upheld most of the ACA. She was also the last Democratic governor of Kansas, probably ever.
question.clue: This former Secretary of Health and Human Services directed the implementation of the Affordable Care Act and presided over the ACA website's disastrous rollout.

swap.text: This leading candidate to replace Bloomberg as mayor has criticized the stop-and-frisk program for targeting minorities, whom he plans to help with city contract quotas. This progressive featured his biracial son Dante in an ad.
swap.clue: This politician once fatally dropped a rodent named Chuck during a Groundhog Day ceremony, and successfully established a universal free pre-K program in his city.

question.text: The CEO of Hewlett-Packard, at the time, was this woman who would go on to unsuccessfully challenge Barbara Boxer in a 2010 senate race.
question.clue: This former CEO of HP and previous candidate for the Republican presidential nomination ran in 2010 for one of California's Senate seats and, in an open-mic gaffe, criticized the haircut of the Democratic opposition, Barbara Boxer.

swap.leadin: In May 2017 this man issued an apology to the Chobani Yogurt Company for his allegation that a plant of that company was involved in a child abuse ring and was responsible for rises in tuberculous cases.
swap.text: Name this far right-wing radio host and conspiracy theorist, known for spreading his views through InfoWars.com. This man claims that Donald Trump personally called him the day after being elected to thank him for his campaign efforts.

question.text: After capturing nineteen percent of votes in the 1992 election, this Texas businessman founded the Reform Party, under whose banner he ran again in 1996.
question.clue: That company was bought by General Motors in 1984 and is Electronic Data Systems.

swap.text: The head of the Judiciary Committee during the Bork nomination was this man, a Senator from Delaware from 1973 until 2009, when he took a higher position in the executive branch.
swap.clue: After his opponent claimed that tax cuts in the 1960s led to economic growth in a 2012 debate, this man asked him, "Oh, now you're Jack Kennedy?"

question.leadin: Answer the following about writings on genocide and civil war.
question.text: This woman wrote A Problem from Hell about American foreign policy on genocides in the 20th century. She was the U.S. Ambassador to the UN from 2013 to 2017.

swap.text: This Supreme Court justice wrote majority opinions striking down moments of silence in Wallace v. Jaffree and prayer at football games in Santa Fe v. Doe. He replaced William O. Douglas on the bench in 1975.
swap.clue: This Supreme Court justice who retired in 2010 and was replaced by Elena Kagan.

question.leadin: Answer questions about the doomed Equal Rights Amendment.
question.text: This founder of the Eagle Forum campaigned to "Stop the Equal Rights Amendment" as it would eliminate nebulous "privileges" and force women into unisex bathrooms. Five states rescinded their ratifications after her anti-ERA campaign began. Her son Andrew runs the website Conservapedia.
question.clue: This person likened "using an atomic bomb to exterminate mice" to legislation sponsored by Michigan representative Martha Griffiths.

swap.text: Earlier, this 1980 Supreme Court case ruled that patents on genetically-modified organisms, such as the namesake General Electric employee's patent on an oil-metabolizing bacterium, are valid.
